projectDetails.description: Starknet is a permissionless Ethereum Layer 2 zk-rollup that leverages STARK proofs and the Cairo language to deliver scalable, low-cost smart contracts.

reviews.text: Starknet is a layer-2 ZK-rollup on Ethereum for scalable dApps, using STARK proofs for security. Launched in 2021 by StarkWare, it supports Cairo language. In 2025, it has a thriving ecosystem with DeFi and games. The network is permissionless, with low fees. It’s advanced but has a learning curve.

Starknet is an L2 (blockchain scaling solution) platform developed by Starkware. It recently connected with Bitcoin Runes and could become an L2 platform for Bitcoin, similar to ETH. It's likely to become an L1 platform in the future. This is certainly a possibility, and there's already a significant amount of BTC on the network. The network's native token is strk. I'm an active user of the network. Its founder is also the founder of Zcash. Starknet's goal is to reduce congestion on Ethereum, increase transaction throughput, and lower gas fees. It achieves this through a roll-up system called zk-stark.

Starknet is an Ethereum Layer-2 using STARK based zk-rollups. It provides on-chain validity proofs that the experts say are quantum secure and runs entirely trustlessly on Ethereum. In 2025 Starknet launched its staking token STRK (used for fees, staking, governance) and many DeFi apps, around 200 projects (DEXes like Ekubo, lending like Vesu, plus BTC bridges) are active. Starknet can batch up to thousands of transactions with cryptographic proofs for efficiency. Recent upgrades include Bitcoin staking integration and the S-Two prover

Starknet is a high speed Ethereum layer 2 scaling solution that uses Quantum resistant zero knowledge Scalable, Transparent Arguments of Knowledge (ZK STARK) proof for validating transactions The protocol has its own native account abstraction capability. Starnet was built using the Cairo programming language which makes it natively non EVM compatible. The protocol was founded by experienced team members backed by tier 1 VCs like Paradigm, Pantera Capital and Founders fund in addition to a grant from Ethereum Foundation. In my opinion, the protocol has a sound fundamental but introduction of new programming language, EVM incompatibility and intense competition from other layer 2 are the main causes of concern about the project.

Starknet feels like a technically elegant Layer 2 I respect that it brings ZK proof security and a native language Cairo for smart contracts. It promises true Ethereum level security with very low fees, which is exciting. Still, to me it seems underutilized. There was a huge user surge around its token airdrop, but activity collapsed afterward daily users fell by about 90% and fees by 99%. That makes me wonder if it can sustain real usage outside of incentives.

Starknet is one of the most serious zkrollup projects on Ethereum. The tech behind it is advanced, and the team is clearly building for the long game. The network focuses on security, scalability, and zero knowledge proofs and even though the ecosystem is still growing, Starknet feels like a chain that wants to solve real problems, not chase hype.
 The only thing is, it’s still early in terms of smoothness and user experience. Some things feel slow or technical for everyday users, but overall, the direction is strong.
